plan.title: AD lesional vs control: 12-sample RNA-seq QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is pre-test quality control only: how do the twelve skin samples (6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, 12,000 genes x 12 samples of raw Salmon gene-level counts in counts.csv, with condition labels in metadata.csv) look, and is sample_01 — flagged at roughly 4x below median library size — usable. No differential testing is planned, so the plan contains no model, no contrast, and no enrichment. Step T1S1 loads the counts and metadata, checks the sample-name join, and computes the depth summary: total library size and number of detected genes per sample, plus each sample's size factor, so sample_01's depth is quantified rather than asserted. Step T1S2 builds the structure view on the same DESeqDataSet: a blind variance-stabilizing transform (blind so the condition labels do not shape the picture), PCA on the 500 most variable genes coloured by condition, and a Euclidean sample-to-sample distance heatmap with hierarchical clustering. Step T1S3 turns those two outputs into an explicit keep-or-drop verdict on sample_01, judged on whether it clusters with its own condition group and whether its depth still supports gene detection — not on depth alone, since median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth and a low-depth sample is down-weighted rather than biased. The verdict step must state its reason and must not silently delete the sample. Splitting depth (T1S1) from structure (T1S2) keeps each script small and lets the verdict step cite both independently.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, Euclidean sample distance heatmap, library sizes and detected genes
QC verdict report on sample_01 with reproducibility record
